signals: one zone (demo), 3 files, ~30 lines: fits T0 by size
additive CLI command; existing commands and todo.json shape untouched
the new command deletes a user item on explicit request (no undo) — 'data deletion' signal, so classified up from T0 to T1
usage string (the CLI's only user-facing contract) gains a line; not a breaking contract change
no migrations, auth, infra, lockfiles or serialized resources touched
unknowns: behaviour of `todo remove` with no id argument (request only specifies unknown ids)
whether a removed id may later be reused by `todo add` (current id assignment is max+1)
whether `removed <id>` should echo the argument as typed or the stored numeric id (e.g. `remove 01`)

questions.text: What should `todo remove` do when no id is given at all?
questions.default: Mirror the existing `todo done`: any id that matches no item, including a missing one, is reported as `no item <id>` with a non-zero exit.
questions.why: Only affects an edge case outside the request; the default is consistent with current behaviour and needs no new rule.

questions.text: After removing the item with the highest id, may `todo add` reuse that id?
questions.default: Keep the current id assignment unchanged (max+1), so reuse is possible; ids are not promised to be unique over time.
questions.why: Changing id allocation would touch add and the file format; nothing in the request asks for it.

questions.text: Should removing an item that is already done be allowed?
questions.default: Yes: any existing id can be removed, done or open.
questions.why: The request says 'delete an item by id' without restriction; refusing would need a second error message it does not define.

assumptions.text: Missing id is treated like an unknown id (`no item <id>`, non-zero exit), as `todo done` does today.
Id assignment for `todo add` stays max+1; a removed top id may be reused.
Done items can be removed exactly like open items.
`removed <id>` prints the stored numeric id (as `done <id>` does), not the raw argument text.
The usage line in the CLI and the usage comment at the top of cli.js both mention `todo remove <id>`.
On an unknown id the todo.json file is not rewritten.
